messages:
alex: Noticing a perf regression with CUDA graphs + multi-GPU. NCCL all-reduce kernels are queued but don't start until graphExec finishes. NCU timeline shows allreduce "queued" while replay runs.

maria: repro steps? which commit/branch and flags?

alex: Repro on v0.14.2-rc. Command I used:
```
./bin/serve --model gpt-j-8 --gpus 8 --batch 4 --seq 2048 --cuda-graphs=1
ncu --timeline --target-pids=$(pgrep run) --kernel-name-regex ncclAllReduce
```
Trimmed NCU note: "ncclAllReduce queued on stream 3 at 42.1ms, stayed idle until 89.3ms (graph replay window)".

jon: Did we change capture streams recently? We usually capture inference on stream 0 and leave prefetch/allreduce on other streams to overlap.

alex: We still capture on stream 0. Pattern I see:
- KV prefetch memcpys + kernel launches on stream 3
- cudaGraphCapture on stream 0 (capture active)
- cudaGraphLaunch(graphExec) at 38ms
- ncclAllReduce was queued at ~42ms on stream 3 but didn't execute until ~89ms after graphExec completed
This serializes critical collectives and kills throughput.

sam: Hypothesis: events/kernels recorded inside the captured graph are not visible to external streams until replay completes, so any streamWaitEvent that references an event recorded by the captured graph will effectively be delayed until the graph finishes.

maria: Can you try moving the NCCL ops into the captured graph or move prefetch into capture to see if it overlaps then?

alex: Moving prefetch into capture does make the allreduce run during replay (no stall) but increases replay latency and makes the graph much bigger (+6ms on replay). Not a good tradeoff for multi-tenant latency SLOs.

jon: Short-term mitigation: gate cuda graphs off for multi-GPU and long sequence lengths (>1024). Longer term we need a solution that preserves overlap without blowing up graph size.

sam: There might be CUDA APIs to bridge captured graphs and external streams (cudaGraphHostNode, external semaphores, cudaEventCreateWithFlags). NV driver semantics around events-in-capture are subtle. We should open an NV support case with the exact timeline.

alex: I ran a focused microbench: if an external stream does streamWaitEvent on an event that was recorded inside a captured graph, the wait completes only after cudaGraphExec completes. So the moment the kernel issues the streamWaitEvent matters: waiting on a captured-event causes serialization.

maria: Filed NV case 015-ccv-332 with trace and minimal repro. Attaching NCU traces and the small repro program.

infra-bot: deploy:patch/disable-cuda-graphs-ml-2026 rolled to staging :robot_face:

jon: For an internal engineering path: either 1) move NCCL to be recorded inside the graph (but that couples graphs and collectives), 2) change ordering so events used for wait are recorded with cudaEventDisableTiming/externally visible flags, or 3) disable graphs selectively. Also add telemetry for "cuda_graphs_blocking_ms" so we catch regressions.

alex: I'll push a small patch that disables cuda graphs for multi-GPU configs and add the telemetry probe. Also uploading the repro artifacts here: https://internal.artifacts/trace-1823456789.tar.gz

sam: Thanks. If NV replies with a recommended API change we can prototype host nodes or external semaphores, but let's not rely on a driver bug fix.

maria: Assigning to eng-runtime perf; @jon @alex @sam to follow up. I'll link the NV case to the jira ticket.
